stories.headline: Amazon, Flipkart restructure seller fees, penalties ahead of festival season
stories.bodyText: New Delhi: E-commerce majors Amazon and Flipkart have revised fee and penalty structures for sellers on their platforms in the weeks leading up to the festive shopping season, a move that sellers say adds to the financial burden on small and medium enterprises already operating on thin margins..According to a notice issued by Amazon India on its seller forum, the company has, with effect from August 17, 2026, changed the manner in which it calculates order cancellation fees for sellers using its Easy Ship and Self Ship services..Amazon, Swiggy, InstaMart & BigBasket may lose food licences in Karnataka.Under Easy Ship, sellers store their own products, pack them when they receive an order and then hand it over to the Easy Ship Pickup executive, who then ships the product and ensures timely delivery..In Self Ship, the seller packs and delivers the product themselves, using their own courier or delivery service, with no Amazon logistics involved..The fee, which was earlier based on category-specific referral charges, is now computed as a percentage of the order value..Under the revised structure, sellers are charged 10 per cent of the order value for orders below Rs 10,000, 8 per cent for orders between Rs 10,001 and Rs 50,000, 5 per cent for orders between Rs 50,001 and Rs 1,00,000, and 2 per cent for orders above Rs 1,00,000, with an 18 per cent goods and services tax levied in addition..The fee is applicable both when a seller cancels an order for reasons other than a buyer's request, and when an order is automatically cancelled because the seller does not ship and confirm the shipment within 24 hours of the estimated ship date..In another notice, Amazon said it will increase closing fees across its Fulfillment Center, Easy Ship, and Seller Flex channels with effect from September 7, 2026..A closing fee is charged every time a product is sold on Amazon based on the price range of the product. This fee varies based on the fulfilment channel a seller is using..The fee will rise by Re 1 for products priced up to Rs 500 and by Rs 3 for products priced above Rs 500. The company attributed the increase to higher fuel and logistics costs..Responding to notices on Amazon's seller forum, some sellers said cancellations were at times caused by factors outside their control, such as delivery personnel failing to arrive for a scheduled pickup, and questioned why cancellation fees should apply to the seller in such instances..Another seller said the difference in total fees between sellers using Amazon's fulfilment network and those on Easy Ship could be as high as Rs 45 per unit on comparable orders, which the seller said creates an unfair competitive situation..Zero-commission to healthy mode: Flipkart enters food delivery race, takes on Zomato and Swiggy.An email query to Amazon did not elicit a response. Flipkart, meanwhile, has put in place a three-tier penalty structure for lapses in order fulfilment, effective August 23, 2026..Under this structure, a shipment not made ready for pickup by the committed Dispatch By Date (DBD) attracts a fine of Rs 30 per shipment. An order cancelled by the seller, or automatically cancelled after three missed dispatch deadlines, attracts a fine of Rs 60 per shipment. Where an order is both delayed and subsequently cancelled, the penalty rises to Rs 90 per shipment..Under the earlier regime, a DBD breach could result in the seller's account being locked for a period of time, which had a relatively greater impact on the seller's business..New sellers on Flipkart, up to three months from the start of their selling journey, will not be impacted by the this policy..The new structure was aimed at inculcating better seller behaviour and encouraging sellers to plan better, with the objective of improving customer experience, people aware of the development told PTI..They said sellers were also rewarded for maintaining good DBD compliance, with benefits such as faster settlement of payments and complimentary advertising credits..Vinod Kumar, Trustee of the Forum for Internet Resellers, Sellers and Traders (FIRST INDIA), said Indian online sellers recognise the need for timely fulfilment and high customer service standards, but that the recent increase in cancellation, dispatch and other seller penalties by major e-commerce marketplaces, particularly ahead of the festive season, was a matter of concern for MSMEs already facing thin margins and rising costs..Kumar said not every cancellation or delay was caused by the seller, citing logistics failures, platform issues, demand spikes and customer-related factors as other possible causes.."Sellers should not become the default financial shock absorbers of the e commerce ecosystem. Marketplaces must ensure transparent attribution of responsibility, reasonable and proportionate penalties, adequate advance notice of fee changes and a simple mechanism to challenge wrongful charges. The objective should be to improve fulfilment while making digital commerce more, not less, viable for small businesses," Kumar added.

stories.headline: Canada will announce retaliatory tariffs against U.S. on August 25, official say
stories.deck: Mark Carney said on August 24 that Canada may need to move away from matching U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar and instead use more targeted retaliation aimed at protecting Canadian workers and businesses
stories.bodyText:
Canada will announce retaliatory tariffs against the United States on Tuesday (August 25, 2026), an official familiar with the plans told The Associated Press, escalating a trade fight that has sharply worsened since negotiations with the Trump administration collapsed.
The official spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the plans publicly.
Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that Canada may need to move away from matching U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar and instead use more targeted retaliation aimed at protecting Canadian workers and businesses.
President Donald Trump escalated the dispute again on Monday (August 24, 2026), telling Canadian leaders to “fall in line” or face consequences “far WORSE” than tariffs already imposed and threatening new 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts and steel.
Mr. Carney accused Washington of trying to subordinate Canada and said U.S. trade demands had confirmed Canada's fears that the United States was seeking to dismantle major Canadian industries.
“An attitude at the negotiation table that Canada is a subsidiary of the United States” is “not something we're going to accept,” Mr. Carney said.
Mr. Carney was even more blunt in French.
“We learned during the negotiations that the Americans want to destroy our major industries, including autos, steel and aluminium,” Mr. Carney said. “That was one of the main reasons we said no. It was a bad deal.”
The fiery words from both sides show how U.S.-Canada relations have deteriorated since Mr. Carney walked away from trade negotiations with the Trump administration late Friday (August 21, 2026), triggering the President's threatened 50% tariffs the next day on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.
Carney cast doubt on the U.S.'s reliability as a partner, saying Canada was finding reliable partners “everywhere in the world, except in the United States. Except in the United States. And Russia.”
Trump unleashes personal attacks on Canadian leaders
Mr. Trump on Monday (August 24, 2026) came back with further tariffs, warning that he would impose them on Canada's auto industry beginning next year.
“Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” Mr. Trump wrote on social media, criticising what he called the country's “ridiculously high tariffs” on American farmers.
Mr. Carney said Washington's auto-sector proposals would gradually have the effect of dismantling Canadian production.
“This is the most successful automotive partnership in history,” Mr. Carney said, referring to the deeply integrated Canada-U.S. industry.
Meanwhile, Ontario Premier Doug Ford unleashed his own tirade. In an interview with The Associated Press, he said Mr. Trump had underestimated Canadians' willingness to endure economic pain rather than give in to U.S. pressure.
“We're all in,” Mr. Ford said. “Up here, we're at a fever pitch; everyone's in for an economic war. They know they're going to have to sacrifice.” Mr. Trump responded in a social media post by attacking Mr. Ford personally, calling him “the less charismatic, intelligent, and overall unimpressive brother of the late, great, Rob Ford,” and once again referring to Canada's Prime Minister as “Governor Carney.”
Mr. Ford dismissed the insults: “If you think an insult from him hurts me? Well, bring it on, buddy, I'm ready.” Mr. Ford is a Progressive Conservative whose party differs from that of Mr. Carney, a Liberal, but the two underscore broad political unity in Canada over the trade fight with Mr. Trump.
Ford threatens critical minerals and electricity
Ford said “everything is on the table” if the dispute worsens, including cutting off electricity and critical minerals from Ontario.
Critical minerals are increasingly important to U.S. national security and manufacturing. The Pentagon has sought more secure supplies of minerals used in military aircraft, missiles, munitions and electronics as Washington tries to reduce reliance on China, which dominates the mining or processing of several strategically important minerals.
Ford said Canada should also consider increasingly severe retaliation if Mr. Trump continues targeting Canadian industries, including oil and potash, while Ontario could raise electricity prices or stop sending power south.
“We power 1.5 million homes and businesses,” Mr. Ford said. “Everything's on the table. I'll do whatever it takes.” Mr. Ford has used electricity as leverage before. During an earlier phase of the dispute, Ontario imposed a 25% surcharge on electricity exported to Michigan, Minnesota and New York.
Mr. Trump responded by threatening to double tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium before both sides backed away.
Auto industry becomes a central battleground
Mr. Ford accused Mr. Trump of not simply seeking a better trade deal but aiming to hollow out Canadian industries and move production south.
Mr. Ford said Mr. Trump wants to make Canada a vassal state.
“He wants to bleed out every single sector and bring them down to the U.S.,” Mr. Ford said.
The auto sector is especially important to Ontario, the centre of Canada's vehicle manufacturing industry. Plants and suppliers in Ontario are tightly integrated with factories in Michigan and other U.S. states, with parts routinely crossing the border multiple times during production.
Automakers including Ford, General Motors and Stellantis operate major assembly plants in Ontario, and the wider supply chain supports tens of thousands of jobs. Mr. Trump's new threat of a 50% tariff on Canadian vehicles and parts puts that sector directly at the centre of the escalating dispute.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that “the only reason Canada has auto production in the first place” was because of the 1960s Auto Pact, under which Canada used access to its market to encourage vehicle production north of the border.
Ford says he opposed preliminary deal
Mr. Ford also disclosed that he had opposed the preliminary agreement Mr. Carney was considering before Canada walked away from negotiations, and that he was unwilling to restore American liquor to Ontario store shelves as part of an agreement.
“I wasn't going to put the booze back on the shelves,” Mr. Ford said. “I was ready to go out there and call a press conference … and say I'm not buckling over.”
Mr. Ford said he understood Washington had sought language late in the negotiations that would have restricted Canada's ability to negotiate trade agreements with other countries without U.S. approval. Mr. Carney has called that demand unacceptable and a question of Canadian sovereignty.
Mr. Carney said the dispute also exposed a deeper divide over language and culture, saying protections for French and Canadian culture that Washington views as trade irritants are considered fundamental rights in Canada.
“Who does he think he is?” Mr. Ford said of Mr. Trump. “You gotta be kidding.”

stories.headline: Youth Morcha storms DM office highlighting critical gaps in schools, questions FIR on activist
stories.deck: The group reached the administration after a case was filed against one of its members, Rajat Singh, for showing the poor condition of government schools on camera in Deoria
stories.bodyText:
Activists of Justice Morcha, a forum of youths pushing the issues of employment and education in Uttar Pradesh, on Monday (August 24, 2026) reached the District Magistrate (DM) office in Deoria, demanding improvement of critical gaps in basic school infrastructure
The group reached the administration after a case was filed against one of its members, Rajat Singh, for showing the poor condition of government schools on camera in Deoria.
“Many activists of the Justice Morcha reached the office of DM Deoria. A case was filed against our colleague Rajat for showing the poor condition of government schools on camera. Today, when Rajat and his colleagues reached the District Magistrate’s office regarding this matter, the District Magistrate immediately left the office,” said Abhinav Mishra, who claims to be associated with the forum.
“We are only demanding improvement of critical gaps in basic school infrastructure. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath claims that the picture of government schools has changed. If the picture of schools has really changed, then why are cases being filed to show the ground reality? Is the Kayakalp scheme also running only on paper? If officials are looting public money under the nose of the Chief Minister, then who will take responsibility for it,” he asked.
On August 22, the police in Deoria booked Mr. Singh, a member of the group, on charges of entering a primary school in Gauribazar’s Damar Bishwa village without authorisation and spreading misinformation. The police registered the First Information Report (FIR) on a written petition submitted by Gauribazar’s block education officer, Vinay Sheel Mishra.
The FIR was registered under sections 329(4): house trans pass and 353(2): circulating false statements, rumours, or alarming reports—including via electronic media—with the intent or likelihood of promoting feelings of enmity or hatred, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
The Congress reacted sharply to the police action, calling it a nefarious attempt to silence youth voices. “Under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government, over one lakh schools have been closed; only in Uttar Pradesh, roughly 25,000 schools are shut. Pupils hailing from marginalised social groups like the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Scheduled Castes (SCs) are being forced out of the education system,” said Ajay Kumar ‘Lallu’, a senior U.P. Congress leader.
“Youths are raising voices against this injustice. Filing an FIR is a nefarious attempt to silence voices. The fact is, in the name of infrastructure development, organised loot is ongoing in the State. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP want to deprive poor people from the ambit of education,” he added.

briefs.headline: TCS to buy Porsche's IT consultancy for over Rs 3,500 crore
briefs.deck: TCS to buy Porsche's IT consultancy for over Rs 3,500 cr
briefs.bodyText: The country's largest IT services firm, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), on Monday said it will acquire sports car manufacturer Porsche's management and IT consultancy subsidiary MHP for over Rs 3,574 crore ($373.42 million). The acquisition is expected to be completed within 3-4 months..MHP, headquartered in Ludwigsburg, near Stuttgart, Germany, is a leader in automotive and industrial consulting in Europe, and has expertise in business consulting, digital transformation, AI, SAP transformation, manufacturing digitalisation, connected and software-defined mobility. The company’s turnover as on CY2025 stood at $865.86 million, and it employs over 4,500 people..In a BSE filing, TCS said the acquisition will anchor a long-term AI transformation partnership between the company and Porsche. To enable this partnership, Porsche has signed a five-year strategic deal with MHP and TCS amounting to $1.46 billion..TCS launches agentic AI platform to transform drug development .As part of the deal, TCS will establish a dedicated AI Mobility Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Porsche to drive innovation across manufacturing, engineering, operations and customer experience. TCS’ expertise provides a strong foundation to scale AI transformation and deliver business outcomes for Porsche’s organisation and its mobility ecosystem. Also, the acquisition will strengthen TCS’ presence in the German market and amongst European automotive and industrial customers, the company said in a statement..The sports car manufacturer will sharpen its strategic focus by concentrating firmly on its core business. In a statement, Porsche said that the aim is to further advance its digital transformation and tap into additional potential across the entire value-chain.."Porsche is taking another important step in its strategy to focus resolutely on its core business with the transfer of MHP to TCS,” Michael Leiters, Chairman of the Executive Board of Porsche, said. “At the same time, we are gaining a strategic partner in TCS. By combining Porsche's automotive expertise with TCS's digital technology and AI capabilities, we will further strengthen our innovative power, increase efficiency and boost our competitiveness in an increasingly data- and software-driven world of mobility," he added..K Krithivasan, CEO and MD, TCS, said, “As AI, software, and data redefine the automotive industry, this partnership brings together TCS’ capabilities in AI, engineering, technology and business transformation with MHP’s strong automotive consulting expertise."

briefs.headline: Footpath eviction row: Bengal minister defends actions after posting video
briefs.deck: Footpath eviction row: Bengal minister defends actions after posting video
briefs.bodyText: Kolkata: After a weekend of receiving flak over her on-camera efforts to remove a footpath-dwelling family — including a woman who was seen boiling milk, apparently for her grandchild — in Kolkata, West Bengal's Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul on Monday accused her critics of trying to thwart the BJP government’s drive to clean up the city and its pavements.The fashion designer-turned-politician said the controversy had wrongly focused on the milk rather than the larger issue of encroachment. She also pointed to the possibility of an accident, with vehicles moving close to the pavement while a stove was burning nearby.She had posted a video of the incident on Facebook on Saturday, in which she — with an entourage of police and media personnel — was seen asking the woman: "Why are you cooking on the footpath?”The visibly unnerved woman replied that she was "just boiling milk for the baby”, to which Paul removed some of the family's belongings and asked: “Why will you boil milk for the baby on the pavement? Is this a place to set up home?”.‘Footpath may be clear, but walking is impossible’: Bengaluru residents flag broken paths. Paul had conducted similar "raids" earlier — typically with journalists in tow — against unorganised markets, hotels, and malls with inadequate fire-safety measures, small businesses encroaching on pavements, and unregulated car parking.But her latest drive drew flak, with critics saying her actions lacked a humane touch. The backlash came not only from the ruling BJP’s political opponents but also from poets, singers, actors, and cultural activists.Actor Sreelekha Mitra asked why a grandmother trying to heat milk for a child should be treated the same as someone occupying a pavement space for commercial purposes.National Award-winning actor Riddhi Sen was more scathing, saying it had become “normal” for many citizens to accept politicians accused of serious wrongdoing in positions of power.Poet and cultural activist Srijato responded with verses that captured the family’s precarious existence.Legislator and the Opposition Trinamool Congress (TMC)'s general secretary Kunal Ghosh visited Park Street on Sunday and met the elderly woman, her daughter, and the child. The adults told him that their husbands had abandoned them, and that the police had now threatened to forcibly evict them.Ghosh visited the nearest police station and requested the cops not to force the family to leave without first finding them shelter.“My party colleagues and I are willing to take responsibility for that family. We can arrange shelter for them at the home of one of our party colleagues, provide them with food, and arrange education for their children. This much, at least, we can do,” TMC chairperson and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee said on Monday.The All-India Democratic Women’s Association (AIDWA), affiliated with the CPM, also condemned Paul's conduct. Its West Bengal-unit president Jahanara Khan and state secretary Monalisa Sinha demanded that the minister publicly apologise for the way she treated the woman.

briefs.headline: Around 40 dead in gang attack near Haiti’s capital
briefs.deck: In a statement issued after the attack, the office of Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime expressed “deep compassion” for the bereaved families and all the victims
briefs.bodyText:
Gang members attacked displaced people huddling inside a church near Haiti’s capital, killing around 40, some of them execution-style, the mayor told AFP on Monday (August 24, 2026).
“We have counted around 40 bodies. Searches are continuing. Some people are still missing,” after the attack Sunday night (August 23, 2026) in the town of Kenscoff in the hills above the capital, its mayor Massillon Jean said.
He described “a night of terror” in a town plagued for months by gang violence.
Mr. Jean said that among other places the assailants targeted a site housing people who had already fled violence.
“The bandits raided a displaced persons camp located in a church. They executed several people. There are fatalities and dozens of wounded. Some people were abducted by the criminals,” Mr. Jean said.
In a statement issued after the attack, the office of Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime expressed “deep compassion” for the bereaved families and all the victims.
The government also announced that reinforcements would be sent to restore security in the area.
Kenscoff, a mountainous municipality southeast of the Haitian capital, has for several months been the scene of clashes and incursions by armed groups seeking to expand their control.
Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, has for years suffered from chronic political instability, natural disasters, corruption and violence from powerful gangs that carry out rampant killings, rapes, looting and kidnappings. The gangs control much of the capital city.
Nearly 1.5 million Haitians are currently displaced in a country of about 11 million, and more than five million are facing severe food insecurity, according to UN figures.
The crisis worsened in early 2024, when gangs launched a wave of violence that forced the unelected Prime Minister to resign.
Haiti has not held any kind of election since 2016. Its last president, Jovenel Moise, was assassinated in July 2021 and not replaced.
A general election is scheduled for December of this year.
Published - August 25, 2026 04:36 am IST

briefs.headline: Tejasvi Surya urges Governor to return parks bill, flags threat to Lalbagh, Cubbon Park
briefs.deck: Surya urges Guv to return parks bill, flags threat to Lalbagh & Cubbon Park
briefs.bodyText: Benagluru: Bangalore South MP L S Tejasvi Surya on Monday wrote to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot, urging him to withhold assent to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, 2026, and refer it back to the state legislature for reconsideration, arguing that the law could open up protected park land to diversion for other purposes..The Governor’s assent is crucial for the bill, which has been passed by both Houses of the legislature..In his four-page letter, Surya said the amendment raised “serious constitutional, environmental and public interest concerns” and urged the Governor to exercise his powers under Article 200 of the Constitution to return it to the legislature..Tejasvi Surya writes to CM DK Shivakumar on short tunnel project at Hebbal.The amendment permits the use of government park land for various public purposes and allows the state government to alienate park land by way of sale, lease, gift, exchange, mortgage or otherwise, subject to an overall ceiling of 5% of the total area of land or buildings comprised in government parks and gardens..Surya said the provision could put around 65.4 acres of park spaces in Bengaluru at risk of diversion. He pointed specifically to Lalbagh and Cubbon Park, which together account for around 437 acres and are preserved under the Act..“At 5%, this could potentially place 12 acres of Lalbagh and 9.85 acres of Cubbon Park, or nearly 22 acres from these two iconic green spaces alone, at risk of diversion,” he stated..The MP said the proposed tunnel road project would require around 1.92 hectares, or nearly five acres, of Lalbagh for construction of the tunnel and shaft. The project’s DPR, he added, envisages parking and a commercial complex around the shaft..He also flagged the proposed Hebbal short tunnel, which would require approximately 3.45 acres of Hebbal Lake, describing the lake as a crucial aquifer and an ecologically important green space..Surya termed the amendment to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, “retrogressive and not in the public interest”.

briefs.headline: For Karnataka government, Adani is a contractor: Priyank Kharge
briefs.deck: For govt, Adani is a contractor: Priyank
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Home Minister Priyank Kharge has defended Chief Minister D K Shivakumar’s closed-door meeting with billionaire business Gautam Adani..“For us, Adani is a contractor. We just want law followed,” he said..Industrialist Gautam Adani meets Karnataka CM Shivakumar, BJP flays Cong on its 'double standard'.“If Adani bags tenders lawfully, so be it,” he said. “What’s BJP’s stand on tunnel road? Will they oppose it, now that it’s being awarded to Adani?” he said.

briefs.headline: Trump moves toward levying new tariff on China for flooding market with cheap goods
briefs.deck: Donald Trump is considering setting the new tariff at 7.5%, according to sources
briefs.bodyText:
United States President Donald Trump is moving toward levying a new tariff on China that would penalise the world's second-largest economy for flooding the global market with underpriced goods, according to three people familiar with the matter.
Two of the people who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations still being finalised said Mr. Trump is considering setting the new tariff at 7.5%. It's a level administration officials believe would not endanger the one-year trade truce between Washington and Beijing or a planned White House meeting between Mr. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping expected to take place in late September.
The move, if finalised, appears to be a calibrated effort by the White House to work around a Supreme Court decision earlier this year that struck down Trump's plan to implement a sweeping, high-tariff scheme not seen since the 1930s.
After that decision, the Trump administration announced in March it was launching formal investigations targeting excess industrial capacity and forced-labour regulations in China and other nations.
It isn't clear if the U.S. administration is also nearing its decision in its probes of the other economies that it announced it was investigating for unfair trade practices, including the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Mexico, Japan and India.
The White House and the U.S. Trade Representative's office did not respond to requests for comment on the tariff deliberations, which Bloomberg News reported earlier on Monday (August 24, 2026). The Chinese embassy in Washington also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The excess industrial capacity probe of China was initiated under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to levy tariffs against nations that discriminate against U.S. companies or commerce.
New tariff would come on top of existing on China
The people familiar with the deliberations stressed that Trump could still change his mind on the new tariff on China.
It would come on top of tariffs of 10% to 12.5% announced last month for 60 economies around the globe that the Trump administration accused of failing to effectively enforce a ban on goods produced with forced labour.
Many countries, including China, protested that move, which took effect just as the clock ran out on temporary tariffs Mr. Trump had turned to after the Supreme Court in February struck down sweeping “reciprocal” tariffs he levied on nearly every U.S. trade partner.
China last month pushed back against claims of overcapacity, anticipating that the US would soon release results of its probe and impose new tariffs.
Massive capacity in a slew of Chinese industries, from autos to solar panels, cement and steel manufacturing, has drawn increased attention from Beijing's trading partners in recent years.
Although China's own leaders have prioritised rebalancing the economy, slowing domestic demand has prompted companies to expand into overseas markets. Surging exports pushed China's trade surplus to a record of nearly $1.2 trillion last year.
China has never sought a large trade surplus, the Ministry of Commerce said in a recently published report titled “China's Position on the So-called Excess Capacity Issue.” The deliberations come as the Treasury Department on Monday (August 24, 2026) warned countries doing trade with Iran that new secondary sanctions are in the pipeline aimed at ostracising nations that continue to do business with Tehran. China is Iran's biggest trade partner.
Washington has promised the new sanctions would put even more pressure on an Iranian economy already battered by previous sanctions and a U.S. naval blockade as the U.S. and Israeli war against Iran nears the six-month mark.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's announcement on Monday (August 24, 2026) provided little detail and did not name which countries could face secondary sanctions.

stories.headline: 4.46 crore voters in Karnataka draft rolls; 1.07 crore names deleted
stories.deck: Special campaign to be conducted in areas reporting high numbers of ‘absent, shifted, duplicate, dead’ names
stories.bodyText:
With the removal of over 1.07 crore names, Karnataka’s electorate shrunk to 4.46 crore voters when the draft electoral rolls were published on Monday as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). An overwhelming number of the missing names were marked ‘absent, shifted, duplicate, dead, and others’ (ASDDO).
Announcing the figures at the end of the enumeration phase, Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) V. Anbu Kumar said the electorate comprised over 2.22 crore males, 2.24 crore females, and 2,871 others. Voters can check their names on the CEO’s official website at https://voters.eci.gov.in/download-eroll?stateCode=S10
The CEO said a special campaign will be conducted in areas reporting high ASDDO numbers, where voters will be assisted in filling Form 6 (for inclusion). The dates for the campaign are yet to be announced by the CEO’s office.
As many as 43.81 lakh notices will be served on voters whose enumeration forms contained logical discrepancies or those who could not be mapped. Notices may also be issued if a complaint is filed against a voter or if the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) has reason to suspect that a voter is ineligible.
With the enumeration phase ending, voters are likely to face the same problems they encountered with the ASDDO list. Just as people remained unaware that their names were in the ASDDO list until 12 days before the enumeration phase ended, they now have no way of knowing whether they will receive a notice until one is actually served. “We only have numbers on how many people will receive notices, and the names will not be known until the notice is generated,” the CEO said.
However, the entire process — from an ERO generating a notice to it being served — is to be completed within just seven days. This could become a major hurdle, especially for voters living in another district or city while remaining registered in their native constituency, as the voter must attend the hearing in person.
There is, so far, no online option to check whether a person is likely to receive a notice. The CEO reiterated that names will be known only after a notice is generated.
The process has now placed the burden of saving one’s vote squarely on the voter. Unlike the enumeration phase, when Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were instructed to hand over enumeration forms to voters and a family member above the age of 18 could fill them on the voter’s behalf, BLOs, during this stage, can serve notices on anyone available at the address. The notice will also carry a QR code to submit one of the 11 documents online, but the voter alone must appear for the hearing.
This could pose challenges for sections of voters such as senior citizens, single mothers, women in general, labourers and persons with disabilities, among others.
For instance, within Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits alone, 40,307 voters are above the age of 85, while 829 are above 100. More than 21,400 voters are persons with disabilities.
More polling stations
Following the enumeration phase, the number of polling stations across Karnataka increased after rationalisation. Each polling station will now have up to and not more than 1,200 voters, and where a polling station had more voters, they were shifted to another polling station within a two-kilometre radius, the CEO said. This has resulted in the addition of 1,873 polling stations across the State.
Voters unable to find their names in their current polling station or booth list have been advised to search using their EPIC details, where the updated polling station will be reflected if rationalisation has taken place. They may also check two polling stations before and after their current one.
Regarding notices on logical discrepancies and unmapped status, EROs have been vested with full powers to take a decision. If aggrieved by an ERO’s decision, a voter can appeal to the DEO/DC within 15 days. If the response remains unsatisfactory, the voter can appeal to the CEO, the final appellate authority, within 30 days of the first appeal.
While the draft electoral rolls were published at 12 p.m. on Monday, people struggled throughout the day to view and download the rolls, particularly the English versions. While voters were able to access the website, after downloading the rolls, files repeatedly threw up errors such as “error” and “file corrupted.”

stories.headline: 10 Bills passed in Karnataka Legislature without debate amid BJP protest on last day of session
stories.deck: Among the Bills was the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows 5% of park land to be sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged for public utility projects undertaken by government departments, statutory authorities, government companies or local bodies
stories.bodyText:
Ten Bills were tabled and passed by the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Council on Monday (August 24, 2026) without debate, as BJP and JD(S) members continued to protest inside and outside the House demanding the resignation of Minister B. Nagendra, who has been chargesheeted in the alleged embezzlement of funds in the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation.
Among the Bills was the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows up to 5% of park land to be sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged for public utility projects undertaken by government departments, statutory authorities, government companies or local bodies.
The amendment is largely aimed at facilitating infrastructure projects, including the proposed 17.1-km Bengaluru North-South Twin Tunnel Road, which will connect Hebbal with Central Silk Board Junction. If enacted, the law could potentially allow up to 5% of the land at Lalbagh Botanical Garden to be utilised for such projects.
The proposal has already drawn strong opposition from citizen groups, environmentalists and BJP MPs from Bengaluru.
Land previously alienated
The Bill provides for an evaluation mechanism headed by the Additional Chief Secretary, along with designated officers and domain experts, to assess proposals for using park and garden land before making recommendations to the government.
It stipulates that the 5% ceiling will include land previously alienated, while routine development undertaken by the Horticulture Department for its own administrative and allied purposes will remain outside the restriction.
The amendment also provides a legal framework for using small portions of horticulture farms for projects such as post-processing facilities, cold-storage units, production of improved crop varieties and agro-based industries that benefit local farmers, subject to recorded reasons establishing public interest and necessity.
Earlier cases of use of park land
The Bill cites previous instances of park land being used for road widening and metro projects. These include 1,223 sq. metres of the Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park given to the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) for road widening, and 1,135 sq. metres of Lalbagh Gardens, along with a portion of its western compound wall, transferred to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited for the construction of an elevated metro station on R.V. Road.
It also cites portions of Cubbon Park that have been used for metro and other public infrastructure projects.

stories.headline: Bengaluru lakes: New study reveals what happens to the sewage after it is diverted
stories.deck: Bengaluru has seen a notable enhancement in lake water quality thanks to the introduction of diversion channels that block untreated sewage from flowing directly into these water bodies. Despite this positive step, the rerouted wastewater continues into the city's drainage system, presenting challenges downstream. A more holistic approach to the water management system is crucial for sustainable…
stories.bodyText:
A lake may look cleaner. The water may smell better. The black stream of sewage that once entered it may no longer be visible. But where did that sewage go?
That question sits at the heart of a new study on Bengaluru's urban lakes. Researchers who examined eight lakes in the city found that diversion channels can make a clear difference to the water quality of the lake they protect. At the same time, diverting wastewater does not make the wastewater disappear. It can move the problem further along the city's drainage network.
The findings, published in 
Frontiers in Water
 on July 30, 2026, look at an issue that has become increasingly important as Bengaluru tries to restore its lakes: is it enough to keep sewage out of one lake, or does the entire water system need to be considered?
The study was conducted by Sumita Bhattacharyya, Priyanka Jamwal and Laurence Carvalho. The researchers compared lakes with diversion channels, lakes receiving a combination of treated and untreated wastewater, and lakes where there was no structural intervention at the inlet.
The lakes with diversion channels had the cleanest water
The difference was visible in the water-quality measurements. The lakes with complete diversion channels had lower concentrations of several pollutants than lakes without intervention. Their average Water Quality Index score was **93**, which placed them in the study's "Clean" category.
The partially diverted lake also fell into the "Clean" category, with an average score of 83.
For comparison, lakes receiving a mixture of treated and untreated wastewater had an average score of 67, classified as "Slightly Polluted". The lakes without intervention scored an average of 56, placing them in the "Polluted" category.
The researchers measured parameters including dissolved oxygen, suspended solids, nitrogen, phosphorus, chemical oxygen demand and alkalinity. Seven parameters showed significantly lower concentrations in the lakes with complete diversion compared with lakes without intervention.
The reason is relatively straightforward. During the dry season, diversion channels prevent untreated wastewater from entering the lake through the main inlet.
But that is only one part of the story.
The sewage still has somewhere to go
A diversion channel deals with the immediate problem at the lake. It does not, by itself, treat the wastewater.
The study notes that diversion channels can therefore provide a local improvement while pushing the wastewater problem downstream. In a city where lakes and drainage channels are connected, that distinction matters.
The researchers are careful not to suggest that every downstream lake will automatically become polluted because of a diversion channel. Water quality depends on several factors, including the catchment, other pollution sources and what is already entering the water system upstream.
But the basic problem remains: removing wastewater from one lake is different from removing pollutants from the water system. That distinction is particularly important in Bengaluru, where stormwater drains can also carry wastewater during dry periods.
The cleaner lakes had less water too
There was another difference between the lakes. The diversion-channel lakes had lower water levels during the dry season because wastewater was no longer continuously entering them.
That can have both advantages and disadvantages.
Having more empty storage capacity before the monsoon can potentially help a lake accommodate incoming rainwater and runoff. But lower water availability during the dry months can also affect some of the services that a lake provides throughout the year.
The researchers point specifically to activities such as fishing.
Two of the lakes receiving a combination of treated and untreated inflows- Sarrakki and Jakkur- had active fishing during the period studied. Based on interviews with fishing communities, the researchers recorded approximate weekly fish yields of 175 kg at Sarrakki and 75 kg at Jakkur.
The comparison shows why simply asking whether a lake is "clean" may not capture everything that happens after a restoration project.
What happens when treated wastewater enters a lake?
Three of the lakes studied- Sarrakki, Hulimavu and Jakkur- received treated wastewater from sewage treatment plants as well as untreated wastewater entering through storm drains.
Their water quality was better than that of lakes without intervention, although they remained in the "Slightly Polluted" category according to the study's Water Quality Index.
Sarrakki had been restored between 2020 and 2021 and had settling tanks and constructed wetlands at its inlets. It recorded better water quality than Jakkur. The researchers also noted that Jakkur's treatment infrastructure had not been adequately maintained in recent years.
This matters because wastewater treatment is not simply about installing a plant and moving on. The performance of the system also depends on how the infrastructure is operated and maintained.
Why the researchers say Bengaluru cannot treat every lake in the same way
One of the more interesting points in the study is that there is no single intervention that serves every purpose. If the immediate objective is to prevent untreated sewage from entering a particular lake, a diversion channel can work.
But a lake also has other functions. It may store rainwater, support aquatic life, provide habitat for birds and other species, contribute to groundwater recharge or support fishing.
What works for one of these functions may not necessarily produce the same result for another. The researchers therefore argue that lake restoration needs to be linked to the intended function of the lake and the wider catchment.
They identify effective wastewater treatment as the preferred long-term approach. They also suggest that additional measures, including constructed wetlands, may be needed in some locations to improve water quality enough to support biodiversity, fisheries and other ecosystem services.
The study has an important limitation
The researchers did not study the lakes throughout an entire year. Water samples were collected three times between February and July 2022, with sampling carried out after at least seven days without rainfall in the catchment. The assessment therefore focused on pre-monsoon conditions.
The authors say this is an initial characterisation rather than a complete picture of how the different interventions perform across all seasons. That distinction is important because Bengaluru's lakes behave differently during the monsoon, when rainfall, runoff and inflows can substantially change the water system.
So, what does this mean for Bengaluru's lakes?
The study does not say that diversion channels are a bad solution. Its findings show the opposite: they can substantially improve the water quality of the lake where untreated wastewater is being kept out.
But the researchers also highlight the trade-off. If the wastewater is diverted rather than treated, it remains part of the wider urban water system. For a city with interconnected lakes, drains and catchments, that makes the question bigger than whether one lake looks cleaner after restoration.
The researchers' conclusion is therefore less about choosing between "diversion" and "no diversion" and more about looking at what the intervention is meant to achieve, what happens to the wastewater afterwards, and how the change affects the rest of the system.
For Bengaluru, the cleaner lake may be the most visible result. The water flowing beyond it may tell the rest of the story.

briefs.headline: SIR in Karnataka: Draft roll out now, here’s how you can check it
briefs.deck: Starting August 24, notices will also be issued to voters whose records have been flagged for logical discrepancies or who could not be mapped to the 2002 electoral rolls.
briefs.bodyText:
The office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, has published the draft electoral rolls for the State. The rolls can be checked here.
However, the process hit a glitch in the initial hours of the release itself, with the website crashing owing to heavy traffic for some constituencies. Citizens who tried to access the rolls were met with error messages or PDFs that would not open.
While many were able to open the Kannada rolls across a few districts and booths, all the English language files were reported to be corrupted. Some could access till their booth/part details but couldn’t download PDFs, while others who clicked the ‘Download’ option were seeing HTML files instead of the PDF.
“They don’t do proper test before releasing. In the morning, they had enabled the link but it took to the bypoll list without any SIR option in the drop down. Later they disabled again (and) opened up without any pdf opening at all... (sic),” an X user remarked.
The draft roll has seen the deletion of more than 1.07 crore names. Bengaluru, which had an electorate of 1.03 crore voters, has seen its electoral roll shrink to 56.11 lakh voters.
Those who find their names marked under the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead or Others (ASDDO) categories can fill out Form 6 and apply for inclusion during the claims and objections period, from August 24 to September 22.
How will notices be served?
Starting today (August 24), notices will also be issued to voters whose records have been flagged for logical discrepancies or who could not be mapped to the 2002 electoral rolls. The notices will be delivered by booth-level officers (BLOs), while hearings will be conducted by Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) or Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs).
Together, 43.8 lakh notices will be served across Karnataka, of which 24.05 lakh are concentrated in Bengaluru alone. BLOs will go from house to house to serve the notices. Any government premises, such as a police station, a government building nearest to the polling station, or gram panchayat office, may be chosen as the hearing venue.
A voter receiving a notice must appear before the ERO in person, even if the required documents are submitted online. A QR code will be printed on the notice, allowing voters to scan it and submit their documents online. The notice will mention the name of the officer, the venue and date of the hearing, along with the reason for which the voter has received it.
A BLO will make only two attempts to serve the notice. If a voter does not attend the hearing, the ERO/AERO will reschedule it only once. The notice can be served to someone on the voter’s behalf, such as a family member or, if no family member is present, a neighbour. However, only the voter can appear for the hearing.

briefs.headline: Gang of six held for killing of Bengaluru medical shop owner
briefs.deck: The deceased was allegedly intercepted by an armed gang in Madiwala traffic signal and hacked to death in full public view on August 22 night.
briefs.bodyText:
The Madiwala police have arrested six people in connection with the murder of medical shop owner, Suhail. The accused have been identified as Adil, a Bandepalya rowdy-sheeter and his associates — Yasin, Abbas, Afivuallah, Shaan, and Syed Farhan
The deceased was allegedly intercepted by an armed gang in Madiwala traffic signal and hacked to death in full public view on Saturday (August 22) night.
Act of revenge
According to the police, the murder was allegedly carried out as an act of revenge for the killing of Adil’s friend Shabbir. Shabbir was murdered in the Bandepalya police station limits in January.
Police suspect that Suhail had allegedly provided financial assistance for Shabbir’s murder and that his brothers were also involved in the killing. Angered by this, Adil allegedly planned Suhail’s murder as a retaliation.
Investigators also suspect that Suhail had threatened his friends that he would assault Adil before Adil could retaliate against him.
After killing Suhail, the accused had reportedly planned to flee to Mumbai. However, Madiwala police tracked them down and arrested all six before they could escape.
The arrested accused are being questioned to establish their individual roles in the murder and the sequence of events leading to the killing.

briefs.headline: Neha Bora slams Congress government in Karnataka over FIRs against students seeking release of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
briefs.deck: AISA chief Neha Bora’s criticism was directed at the Congress government, which, she argued, had extended solidarity to student protests at Jantar Mantar in Delhi against Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, but filed FIRs against students in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
“Political parties who claim to be anti-BJP must lead by example and show what anti-BJP looks like. Instead of providing mere lip service to this anti-fascist agenda, they must show what pro-student politics actually looks like,” All India Students Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora said at the ‘Gen Z on the March’ programme in Bengaluru on Sunday (August 23, 2026), as she condemned the Congress government in Karnataka for filing FIRs against students who raised slogans demanding the release of Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam.
Actor Kishore and musician T.M. Krishna were also part of the programme, which highlighted the new wave of youth politics in India and issues of accountability.
Ms. Bora’s criticism was directed at the Congress government, which, she argued, had extended solidarity to student protests at Jantar Mantar in Delhi against Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, but filed FIRs against students here.
Warning political parties that claim to oppose the BJP, Ms. Bora said that if they behaved like the BJP and treated students and young people the way the BJP did, the young people and students of the country would treat them like the BJP.
However, the “fear felt by the BJP-led Union government is not enough,” she said. “What will be enough is when this government and the BJP-RSS system would have been uprooted from the soil of this country. Only then must we rest,” she said.
Pointing out to recent events in Karnataka, Ms. Bora began by extending solidarity to the students of Azim Premji University (APU), who, she said, had been fighting a “complete crackdown” on democratic discussion on their campus. She referred to students who had recently been suspended for two years by the university for holding a discussion on the 1991 Kunan-Poshpora incident in Kashmir.
She also extended solidarity to organisations in the State fighting against the forced closure of government schools and centralised “KPS magnet schools.”
Recalling the “rage” felt by people during events under the BJP’s tenure, including demonetisation, and the struggles of people fighting injustices and protesting across parts of India, Ms. Bora called on people to “educate, organise and agitate.”
“Rage does not mean violence or anarchy. It means asking yourself what this country needs from you at this moment, and putting your soul into building that country - into taking this country away from the fascists in a way that means the defeat of the BJP, not just in Parliament, but the defeat of the RSS and its ideology within our shared spaces.”
“The Gen Z will fight with all the force of history and forge ourselves a future where there is no place for the RSS, where there is no place for the BJP – not just today, not tomorrow but never in the future.”
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Kishore said that as the movement focused on issues such as paper leaks, there appeared to be a hesitancy to mention certain names, issues, incidents and parts of history in an effort to keep it restricted to the issue of paper leaks.
Referring to objections over taking the names of Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam and raising the slogan “Azadi”, he said, “If our idea of unity requires us to forget certain people, communities, histories, then perhaps we need to examine what kind of unity we are creating.”
He said that while fighting one issue, the movement should not lose sight of other injustices, including Rohith Vemula, the suffering of children and civilians in Gaza, victims of the war in Ukraine and innocent people caught in conflicts and violence across the world.
“We may not be able to solve every one of those problems, but we must retain the capacity to remember them,” he said.
Mr. Krishna spoke about how young people have brought creativity into politics and challenged the common notion of why students should engage in politics, arguing that “everything is political.”

briefs.headline: Adani calls on Karnataka CM, sparks political speculation
briefs.deck: Government sources said that the meeting was unscheduled, and that Mr. Adani, who was attending a private function in Bengaluru South was on his way to the airport, when he dropped in at the Chief Minister’s residence
briefs.bodyText:
A meeting between Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar here on Sunday (August 23, 2026) set off speculation in political circles. While the Chief Minister termed it a courtesy visit, the Adani Group is an interested bidder in the tunnel road project in Bengaluru being pushed by Mr. Shivakumar.
Government sources said that the meeting was unscheduled, and that Mr. Adani, who was attending a private function in Bengaluru South was on his way to the airport, when he dropped in at the Chief Minister’s residence. “It was a courtesy visit since Mr. Shivakumar took over as the Chief Minister recently.”
Incidentally, the Adani Group has emerged as the lowest bidder in the 17.1-km Bengaluru’s North-South twin tube tunnel road connecting Hebbal and Silk Board junction that is estimated to be around ₹17,000 crore. Of the total cost of the project that has been proposed on the build-own-operate-transfer (BOOT) model, the government is expected to invest 40% through viability gap funding through a loan from Hudco. The Adani Group is learnt to have quoted just above ₹22,000 crore for the project.
Taking a dig at the Congress, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok said: “(Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha) Rahul Gandhi has called Mr. Adani a BJP agent. However, the Karnataka government has rolled out a red carpet for Mr. Adani. Have the (Central) Congress leaders given permission for this? So, let him advise Mr. Gandhi properly.”
In response, Mr. Shivakumar told presspersons here: “Mr. Adani paid a courtesy visit after I became the Chief Minister.”

stories.headline: Meiji Seika to push new vaccine with SII in India
stories.bodyText:
TOKYO: Meiji Seika Pharma-owned Medreich Pharma is eyeing inorganic growth and more generics supply from India, while the parent has tied up with 
Serum Institute of India
 (SII) to launch Japanese Encephalitis vaccine in the country.
"SII will take the required approval to provide the vaccine for children in India. Our subsidiary has already marketed this vaccine in Japanese market. Hopefully, next year SII will apply and try to take the approval in India and then they will market this vaccine," Meiji Seika Pharma COO for pharma segment Toshiaki Nagasato said after a meeting with commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal here on Monday. The Japanese company is seeking that the approval should be accelerated.
"SII manufactures at the lowest cost. We believe SII will launch the vaccine at affordable and lowest cost. SII technology offcials also came to Japan to understand the technology in Japan," Nagasato said.
According to WHO, there are three types of Japanese Encephalitis vaccines, which are given to children. Japan has the technology to help combat the disease that it once grappled with and combined with India's low cost manufacturing capability the partnership could help children. 
SII and Meiji Seika Pharma had announced the achievement of the first milestone last April.
Nagasato said the Japanese company is looking to invest into its Indian subsidiary Medreich, which it had acquired in 2014, although he refused to disclose the amount. He said the idea is to help expand the Indian company's generic operations within the country and also for exports to countries, such as UK, Canada and other European and African companies.

stories.headline: Government eyes 3000 crore by selling 6% in Hindustan Copper
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Govt is selling up to 6% in Hindustan Copper at a floor price of Rs 514 per share through an offer for sale (OFS) to mobilise about Rs 3,000 crore. The floor price for the OFS is at an 11.6% discount to the stock's closing price of Rs 573.6 on BSE on Monday. This is the 10th divestment offer in the current fiscal.
According to the company's disclosures on BSE, govt is offering to sell a little over 2.9 crore shares (3% of the company's equity capital) through the OFS, which will open today. Depending on the demand, govt may offer another 2.9 crore shares to investors, it said.
Retail investors will be able to bid on the second day of the offer, that is, Aug 26. "10% of the offer is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares reserved for eligible employees," secretary, DIPAM, govt's divestment department, said through a post on X (formerly Twitter).
Currently, govt holds 66.1% in the copper miner and producer, shareholding data on BSE showed. Post the successful divestment in the company, govt's stake would come down to a little over 60%. DAM Capital Advisors, Emkay Global Financial Services and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities are managing the offer for govt, the OFS notice on BSE showed. This divestment comes within three weeks of the most successful OFS in India.
 On Aug 6, govt closed the offer to sell 10% in life insurance major LIC and mobilised Rs 31,515 crore from the market. It was the biggest such offer in India ever.
Till date in FY27, govt has mobilised Rs 52,716 crore from nine divestments and some receipts from SUUTI. The Budget had set a Rs 80,000-crore divestment target for the current year.

stories.headline: Government lifts ban on wheat exports, cites farmers’ interests amid depressed local prices
stories.deck: India, the world's second-largest wheat producer, had banned wheat exports in May 2022 as part of measures to control rising domestic prices
stories.bodyText:
The government on Monday (August 24, 2026) lifted the export ban on wheat and wheat products with immediate effect and said the decision is aimed at boosting farmers' income amid depressed domestic prices.
Early this year, the government had allowed the export of 50 lakh tonnes of wheat and 10 lakh tonnes of wheat products.
India, the world's second-largest wheat producer, had banned wheat exports in May 2022 as part of measures to control rising domestic prices.
"The export policy of wheat.... is revised from prohibited to free with immediate effect," according to notifications issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
The government has also removed the export ban on wheat flour and other products such as maida, semolina, and wholemeal atta, as per other notifications.
When asked about the decision, Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra told PTI, "The export ban has been lifted in the interest of farmers. The domestic wheat prices are depressed currently. Allowing exports will increase the domestic market prices and encourage good sowing in the coming rabi season, and farmers will get better prices." On the impact of consumer prices, Mr. Chopra said there is adequate stock of wheat available in the country, sufficient to meet the demand and check prices.
The export of wheat, which was allowed earlier through issue of licence, has now been simplified, he added.
Out of 60 lakh tonnes allowed earlier, 2.5 lakh tonnes have been shipped so far, the secretary said.
India's wheat production stood at a record 120.65 million tonnes in the 2025-26 crop year (July-June) as against 117.94 million tonnes in the preceding year.
The Food Corporation of India (FCI), the government's nodal agency for the procurement and distribution of foodgrains, has nearly 49 million tonnes of wheat in buffer stock.
According to government data, the all-India average retail price of wheat stood at ₹31.46 per kg on Monday (August 24, 2026), while the rate of wheat flour at ₹37.3 per kg. The rates of wheat and wheat flour are flat compared to the year-ago period.

stories.headline: ‘Of 25 wealthiest family-run Indian businesses, five held over 60% revenues in two decades’
stories.bodyText:
A study of 25 wealthiest Indian family-run businesses over financial years 2000-2020, revealed that the top five among them, held over 60% of the cohort’s combined revenues, despite liberalisation making markets more competitive. This study appeared in the World Bank Economic Review.
The study titled “Business Groups, Concentration and Market Power in India” published in the World Bank Economic Review authored by Simon Commander, visiting professor at IE Business School, Madrid, Spain among other researchers from different universities, found that Reliance, Adani, Birla, Om Prakash Jindal and Tata Groups put together controlled over 60% of the 25 wealthiest family-run firms’ business revenues between 2001 and 2020. Barring the Birla Group, whose share in the cohort reduced steadily during the study period, the shares of other family businesses increased. Reliance and Adani Groups have consistently constituted at least 20% share in the top 25 family-run businesses’
The study acknowledges that the concentration in the market has reduced and as a result competitiveness has increased after liberalisation. This however has not prevented the large family business groups from dominating the market. The top 25 family business groups constitute over 15% of the Gross Domestic Product–the value of goods and services sold–in 2020, the study observed.
“The paper finds that market concentration has indeed been declining during that period, mainly due to policy-induced shrinkage of the public sector. Concentration has also been falling for the private sector and for the FBGs. Thus, at the NIC-3 level, the proportion of industries with low concentration has risen considerably over the period,” the authors observed. The largest five firms within each NIC-3 industry, controlled more than half of the revenues in around 74% of NIC-3 industries, the study found. NIC 3 refers to a Statistics Ministry classification of industries by specific subsectors.
At the same time, family business groups have also diversified across different sectors, the study found.
The authors concluded that Indian government’s approach of showing preference for some business groups as “national champions” in the period studied may have led to the higher concentration.
“To date, public policy appears to have achieved, at best, limited success in addressing the consequences of this increased concentration for competition, whether in terms of market power in specific sectors or with respect to the level of overall concentration in the economy,” the authors wrote.
Competition policy, taxation or prohibitions will not be as effective in addressing entrenched family business group power in the Indian market, the authors said while suggesting that setting specific limits to the maximum market share that a business group can hold and subsequently divesting when a specified level is reached can be explored as a policy option.
