briefs.headline: Government looks to add more AI partners for digital projects
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt is looking at widening its pool of technology partners for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) projects, with the ministry of electronics and IT reopening empanelment of agencies that can deploy AI/ML resources across govt programmes.
The fresh tender has been issued by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), which functions under MeitY, and seeks to bring more companies onto an existing panel created for AI/ML manpower augmentation and AI-driven project delivery under the Digital India programme.
The move follows the first round of empanelment, in which six companies - Tata Consultancy Services, NEC India, Kyndryl, CoRover, Innefu Labs and Cactus Technology Solutions - were selected to work on govt AI projects. Companies joining through the latest round will have to accept the rate card discovered during the earlier empanelment process, indicating that the exercise is aimed at expanding the vendor base rather than undertaking a fresh price discovery.
NeGD published the reopened Request for Empanelment on Aug 10, with bid submissions scheduled to close on Sept 7. The bids are expected to be opened on Sept 8.
The empanelled companies can be tapped for deployment of AI and machine learning professionals and execution of AI-led projects across government departments and Digital India initiatives.

briefs.headline: Labour survey 2026 likely to track digital, platform workers
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In a first, India's official statistical machinery is likely to provide data on the digital and platform-based workers in the upcoming annual periodic labour force survey (PLFS), a move which will help policymakers assess the true scope and nature of the fast-growing gig workforce in India, an official told TOI.
"In PLFS 2026, data on digital platform workers - a subset of gig workers is being collected among the workers classified in the existing PLFS framework as self-employed, regular wage/salaried or casual workers on an experimental basis. All such workers will be included in the broader self- employed category," the official said. The survey results are expected in March 2027 and will provide the maiden official estimate of the number of people working as food delivery executives, drivers and as a myriad of home service providers, among other things in the country.
Currently, anyone who engages in market activities for profit is covered under the PLFS framework as a worker, though it does not capture data on people engaged in the gig or digital and platform-based work separately, thus making it difficult to identify gig and platform workers among the total workforce. Drawing upon a 2022 NITI Aayog study, a labour ministry think tank VV Giri National Labour Institute in its latest study expects the gig and platform workforce in the country to grow over 6 crores by 2047 - constituting nearly 15% of the total non-agricultural workforce in the country.
"Along with enumeration, other key characteristics of such workers, which will include their earnings, working hours, working conditions will also be captured in the upcoming labour force survey. This will help govt to formulate welfare policies for them and implement the provisions of the social security code," the official added.

briefs.headline: India a safe base, Piyush Goyal tells Japanese investors
briefs.deck: Cites Long List Of Trade Deals, Says Data Is Protected, Intellectual Property Is Secure
briefs.bodyText:
TOKYO: It isn't just high growth and an expanding market that make India an attractive destination for investors. Commerce and industry minister 
Piyush Goyal
 on Monday added India's long list of FTAs and the possibility of Japanese companies using the preferential tariffs to set up a base to it and looking at it as a gateway to the world.
And, he topped it up by positioning India as a safe base for Japanese companies as data is protected, intellectual property is secure and where an entrepreneur does not "go missing only to be found as a professor in some other country". The last three were seen as a dig at China, amid indications that companies, including Google, are looking to shift a part of their mobile manufacturing facility in what has come to be known as "China+1" strategy.
"India is not a plus one country. India stands on its own merits as a trusted partner. We don't steal anybody's technology, we don't copy anyone's intellectual property products and bring it into the market. In India you have a growing middle class, the fastest growing major economy in the globe and most importantly the youthful talent," Goyal said. He also signalled that govt was willing to relax rules, provided it does not result in imports from "one country", which is not conducive for fair trading practices and often supplies goods at predatory pricing.
While Japan has been pushing for deeper ties with countries such as India, the recent trade tussle with China has added to the urgency.
The minister also made a strong case for India as a good fit to address issues that Japan was facing. "One can clearly see that for an economy like Japan, which has very good technologies but not enough people, which has excellent business practices but not enough market, India can be an excellent partner, which provides economies of scale with a large domestic market and India which has opened its doors to international engagement with several FTAs... we are a trusted partner in global supply chains and for Japan to enjoy competitive advantage over other countries, working with India, will give it a natural edge."
As he courted multiple investors, he asserted that govt was willing to address individual concerns that Japanese companies may have and cited two cases on Monday itself when he spoke to officials in India to find a solution to the issues flagged by a semiconductor equipment manufacturer and another by an auto components player.
During another meeting, Goyal urged Japanese steel makers to buy India-made steel for local requirements instead of importing it into the country.
He also said that India is negotiating trade deals with at least eight-nine trading partners that together account for another $15 trillion of GDP. The country's FTAs would eventually cover about 75% of global trade.

briefs.headline: TCS to acquire Porsche arm for $373 million, inks $1.4 billion deal
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: In a mega deal that boosts its manufacturing and AI playbook, TCS will acquire MHP Management, the consulting and technology subsidiary of German sports car maker Porsche, for $373 million. The transaction will also anchor a five-year strategic partnership worth $1.4 billion.
The partnership will focus on driving AI-led transformation across Porsche's engineering, manufacturing, operations, customer experience and enterprise functions, while also developing next-generation automotive technology services and software-defined mobility platforms.
Porsche said the decision is part of its "Sportwagenschmiede 35" strategy, which aims to strengthen profitability and cash flow through 2035. The sports car manufacturer said it plans to sharpen its strategic focus by concentrating on its core business.
TCS, Porsche seal $1.4-billion five-year partnership for AI-led automotive transformation
TCS said its Netherlands subsidiary, Tata Consultancy Services Netherlands, approved the acquisition of MHP's equity shares from Porsche and signed a share purchase agreement for the proposed transaction. The acquisition is subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions and is expected to be completed within three to four months.
The partnership with Porsche will serve as an anchor for TCS's AI transformation strategy and position the leading Indian IT services company as a strategic consulting and technology partner for Porsche, while creating opportunities to expand its offerings among other automotive and industrial customers in Europe.
MHP is a leading automotive and industrial consulting firm in Europe, with capabilities spanning business consulting, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, SAP transformation, manufacturing digitalisation, connected mobility and software-defined mobility. However, MHP will retain its brand and continue to operate as an independent consultancy under its existing name.
TCS CEO K Krithivasan said, "As AI, software, and data redefine the automotive industry, this partnership brings together TCS' capabilities in AI, engineering, technology and business transformation with MHP's strong automotive consulting expertise. Together, we will industrialise AI at scale for Porsche, accelerating innovation across the value chain to deliver intelligent, software-defined mobility experiences of the future."
Dr Michael Leiters, CEO of Porsche, said, "Porsche is taking another important step in its strategy to focus resolutely on its core business with the transfer of MHP to Tata Consultancy Services. At the same time, we are gaining a strategic partner in TCS. By combining Porsche's automotive expertise with TCS' digital technology and AI capabilities, we will further strengthen our innovative power, increase efficiency, and boost our competitiveness in an increasingly data and software-driven world of mobility."

briefs.headline: UPI@10: How platform changed the way we pay
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Nearly one in two real-time payments in the world happen on the UPI platform. From 1.8 crore transactions in FY17, the year it was launched, to 24,162 crore transactions in FY26, UPI transactions have grown 13,000 times.
Today, the payment platform completes 10 years since it went live for general public use after its initial launch by then RBI governor Raghuram Rajan through a pilot test in April 2016. How did the most successful innovation under NDA govt come about?
According to AP Hota, founding chief of National Payments Corporation of India, during whose term most of NPCI's products, including UPI, were launched, the idea originated from a dilemma over how to increase the use of IMPS (Immediate Payment Service). IMPS was a real-time payment platform built by repurposing the national financial switch infrastructure created for ATM transactions which required real-time debits from bank accounts. Before IMPS, electronic payments largely mimicked traditional payments, with transactions taking place in batches.
Initial brainstorming showed that merchants needed to receive money immediately, which cards could not provide. 
While IMPS enabled person-to-person transfers, it was not designed for customers who wanted to pull money.
"UPI began as an attempt to redesign IMPS so as to simplify merchant payments, involve non-bank payment providers, reduce e-commerce payment failures, and adopt open-source technology and APIs. These objectives led us to move away from IMPS and build an entirely new solution, retaining only its proven real-time settlement engine," said Hota.
"Pramod Verma (technology architect who helped design UPI's API-driven architecture and played a key role in shaping its open, interoperable framework) became involved, while Nandan Nilekani was already with us as our technology and public policy adviser. Pramod and Nandan came up with the idea of making the entire system API-driven, with third-party application service providers," said Hota, who worked with banks and fintech companies to expand the network.
Dilip Asbe, current chief of NPCI, who was COO at the time of the launch and led much of the implementation, explained the design in a podcast with Verma in Aug last year. UPI's scale, they said, came from designing it not as a centralised application with a massive database but as a decentralised, open protocol that resolves payment addresses in real time across participating banks.
The architects built advanced capabilities into the core protocol while adopting a phased rollout, starting with basic peer-to-peer transfers before introducing features such as recurring mandates.
While UPI's scale is now measured in billions of transactions, Hota had forecast in his 2017 farewell speech that the platform would achieve a billion transactions a day within a few years.

briefs.headline: Sugar prices fall in the domestic market; concerns remain on price volatility
briefs.bodyText:
With the government’s announcement last week permitting import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar, the domestic prices are cooling down.
However, volatility in domestic sugar prices continues to be a matter of concern.
The current sugar marketing season that began on October 1 last year saw a substantial quantity of sugar sold at ₹38-Rs. 39 a kg (ex-mill price). Prices started going up in January, climbed to ₹48 a kg, and on Monday (August 24, 2026) stood at ₹56 a kg (Maharashtra ex-mill price).
The price was ₹58 a kg (Maharashtra ex-mill) on August 22 and ₹62 a kg on August 21.
An industry source said the ex-mill prices are likely to hover between ₹50 and ₹60 till November - December.
Office bearers of the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) told reporters in New Delhi on Monday (August 24, 2026) that the recent firmness in sugar prices should not be construed as a shortage of sugar in the country.
India’s sugar balance remains fundamentally comfortable, with net sugar production for 2025–2026 (sugar season) estimated at around 279 lakh tonnes (LMT) against domestic consumption of 280–285 LMT, and projected closing stocks of around 35 LMT. Adequate stocks are available to ensure uninterrupted domestic supplies through the transition into the next sugar year.
The recent increase in sugar prices is the result of a convergence of temporary factors, including lower-than-initially-expected production, heightened festive-season demand, market sentiment, and firm international sugar prices, according to the ISMA.
Welcoming the Union Government’s steps to stabilise prices, such as the import of 10 lakh tonnes of duty-free raw sugar, restrictions on holding stocks, and the possible advancement of the 2026–27 crushing season, they said that such measures together constitute a comprehensive package aimed at strengthening market confidence, discouraging speculative holding, and facilitating smooth availability of sugar.
Sugar mill sources say imported sugar, probably from Brazil, will land in Indian ports only by mid-October. The government has also permitted sugar refineries that have stocked sugar imported under an advance licence (for export after value addition) to sell some of the stock in the domestic market.

briefs.headline: Bank unions threaten nationwide strike on September 11 to press for 5-day banking
briefs.deck: If the strike materialises, banking services, would be impacted for four days in many parts of the country
briefs.bodyText:
The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) will begin a nationwide strike on September 11 over the delay in implementing a five-day banking week, differences over performance-linked incentive schemes, and several other pending demands, including pension related issues.
If the strike materialises, banking services, especially in public sector banks, would be impacted for four days in many parts of the country. September 11 is a Friday, and the subsequent two days are bank holidays. September 14 is a holiday in some states for Ganesh Chaturthi.
UFBU, an umbrella body of nine bank employees' and officers' unions, has also threatened a subsequent three-day nationwide strike beginning September 28, coinciding with half-yearly closure.
They have also decided to go on an indefinite strike from October 26 onwards if their demands fall on deaf ears.
The decision was taken at a meeting held on Sunday with the UBFU stating that the government had a “negative attitude” towards key demands.
Pending for two years
On five-day banking, it said the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) agreed to the proposal as part of the 12th Bipartite Settlement/9th Joint Note signed on March 8, 2024, under which working hours were to be increased by 40 minutes from Monday to Friday.
The proposal was subsequently recommended to the government but has remained pending for more than two years, it said.
The unions have also objected to the government's PLI scheme for bank officers of Scale IV and above, saying it differs from the understanding reached with the IBA that performance-linked incentives would be linked to the overall performance of individual banks and would be uniform for employees and officers up to Scale VII.
Under the government's scheme, officers in Scale IV and above could receive PLI of up to 365 days’ basic pay based on individual performance, while workmen employees and officers up to Scale III would receive a maximum of 15 days' basic pay plus dearness allowance, it said.
The issue of PLI is currently under conciliation before the Chief Labour Commissioner (CLC) following the strike call issued by the UFBU and is also pending before the Delhi High Court, it claimed.
The UFBU further alleged that despite the pendency of conciliation proceedings and its offer to hold bilateral discussions with the IBA, the Department of Financial Services (DFS) has advised banks to implement the government's performance-linked incentive scheme.
Crediting of performance-linked incentive under the DFS scheme has now actually commenced in the banks, the UFBU said, alleging that this was in violation of the status quo obligation during conciliation proceedings.
The UFBU argued that the present PLI scheme suggested by the DFS would disproportionately benefit a small section of officers and undermine the principle of uniformity in incentives across cadres.
The residual demands, including updating and improving pensions, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to switch to the old pension scheme (OPS), also remained unresolved.

briefs.headline: Third Wave Coffee raises ₹408 crore in funding led by WestBridge Capital
briefs.bodyText:
Third Wave Coffee, a city-based coffee and food firm, has raised Rs 408 crore in a funding round led by existing investor WestBridge Capital while the round also witnessed participation from Creagis and other angel investors.
The new funding is expected to fuel Third Wave Coffee’s next phase of expansion, with capital directed towards geographic growth in existing markets, building greater density in high-potential cities and strengthening the brand’s ability to serve a wider range of consumer occasions, as per the company.
Third Wave Coffee has accelerated its national footprint by entering Ahmedabad, Mangalore and Agra last year while strengthening its presence across Delhi, NCR, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai and Pune. In June 2026, it entered East India with three cafés in Kolkata. The firm is currently evaluating opportunities in other eastern markets, including Guwahati, Ranchi, Patna and Bhubaneswar.
Rajat Luthra, CEO, Third Wave Coffee, said the brand currently operated more than 240 cafés across India and were aiming to reach 320 cafes by end FY27.
“Over the years, we have built a strong consumer proposition, and our focus remains on scaling the business sustainably, with strong unit economics, healthy store payback operational discipline and a consistent customer experience. This fundraise will help us accelerate our expansion across the country while strengthening new categories, with desserts being an important part of the journey. . Our vision to add 100 new cafes every year; reflects the significant opportunity we see ahead,” he added.

Top seed Woman FIDE Master (WFM) Pratitee Bordoloi emerged as the sole leader in the Asian Junior Girls Classical Chess Championship, scoring a crucial win over Woman Candidate Master (WCM) Aadya Gowda in the seventh round in Mumbai on Monday (August 24, 2026).

Fide Master (FM) M Prishita Gupta strengthened her title challenge with a victory over WFM Nivedita V.C. to reach 5.5 points, joining Leyla in the chasing group. WFM Mariya Kholyavko of Kazakhstan and WCM Dakshita Kumawat drew their encounter and moved to five points.
In the Open Championship, top seed Grandmaster-elect Mayank Chakraborty maintained his sole lead after the completion of seven rounds.
Mayank was held to a draw by International Master Vignesh Advaith Vemula, but the result was enough to take his tally to six out of seven and keep him half a point ahead of the chasing pack.

stories.headline: India's Sriram Balaji, Anirud Chandrasekar crowned Cancun Country Open Doubles title
stories.deck: The champions earned 125 ranking points along with a $9,900 prize, while the runners-up received 75 points and $5,760
stories.bodyText:
N. Sriram Balaji and Anirud Chandrasekar were crowned champions of the second edition of the Cancun Country Open after defeating the Mexican-Belarusian pairing of Miguel Angel Reyes-Varela and Ivan Liutarevich 6-3, 7-6(4) in the final.
Fine margins proved decisive in the defeat of Reyes-Varela and Liutarevich, who conceded just one break of serve throughout the match but were unable to convert their only break-point opportunity, as per the Cancun Country Open website.
The Cancun title is Chandrasekar’s 11th on the circuit and his second of the year. Earlier this season, he won the Busan ATP Challenger 125 alongside Japanese partner Takeru Yuzuki.
This is Balaji’s fifth Challenger title of the year, with his previous four victories coming alongside Neil Oberleitner. The triumph also marks his 15th career title on the Challenger circuit.
The Indian pair produced a solid performance, but Reyes-Varela and Liutarevich matched them closely for much of the opening set.
The decisive moment came in the eighth game, when Balaji and Chandrasekar secured the only break of serve to take control and eventually close out the set 6-3.
They won 68% of points behind their first serve and an impressive 81% behind their second.
The champions earned 125 ranking points along with a $9,900 prize, while the runners-up received 75 points and $5,760.

stories.headline: 'We started poorly': Craig Fulton rues slow start as India crash out of WC semis
stories.deck: India's journey in the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 came to an end with a disappointing 5-3 defeat against Argentina. Struggling with a sluggish start and mounting pressure, the Indian team fell behind early and faced challenges in regaining momentum. A late surge saw them net three goals in the final quarter, but it wasn't enough. Next, they will face off in a playoff for seventh place.
stories.bodyText:
India's hopes of reaching the semifinals of the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 came to an end on Monday after a 5-3 defeat against Argentina in their final Pool E match at the Wagener Hockey Stadium.
India head coach Craig Fulton admitted that his team's slow start and inability to handle the pressure of a must-win game proved costly as Argentina took control early and held on despite a late Indian fightback.
“It was a difficult day today. We didn’t want to end like that. We started poorly, but the second quarter was much better. The third quarter wasn’t good, but then we scored three goals in the last quarter and could have scored the fourth one too from a corner,” Fulton told PTI after the defeat.
“Overall, it was a really strange game. We played at a high level in tournament, but in the big games we have to do better,” he added.
Fulton also acknowledged that the qualification permutations surrounding India's semifinal hopes affected the team's performance.
“There were a lot of permutations going into this game that got the better of us. In the last 10 minutes, we played better hockey. That was a little too late,” he said.
Argentina make India pay for slow start
India's problems began almost immediately as Argentina scored just 41 seconds into the contest. Joaquin Toscani found the net from a tight angle to give Argentina an early lead. The world No. 7 side doubled its advantage in the 16th minute when Nicolas della Torre converted a penalty corner.
India responded through 
Sukhjeet Singh
, who pulled one back in the 10th minute with a field goal after a well-worked move involving Abhishek. India had spells of possession in the second quarter but struggled to make the most of their opportunities in the final third. Neither side managed to score in the second quarter, leaving Argentina 2-1 ahead at half-time.
Argentina pull away in third quarter
India needed a strong second-half response but instead found themselves further behind. Three minutes into the third quarter, Tomas Domene capitalised on a midfield dispossession to make it 3-1. India earned several penalty corners as they searched for a way back, but captain 
Harmanpreet Singh
 could not find a breakthrough.
Argentina then received a penalty stroke just before the end of the quarter after an Indian defensive error. Domene made no mistake from the spot, completing his second goal of the match and putting Argentina 4-1 ahead. The deficit became even steeper in the fourth quarter when Lucas Toscani scored in the 53rd minute to make it 5-1.
India finally found their attacking rhythm late in the match. Sukhjeet Singh scored his second goal in the 58th minute with a clever deflection before Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke two minutes later to reduce the deficit to 5-3.
India then earned another penalty corner in the dying seconds, but Argentina goalkeeper Tomas Santiago made the crucial save as the final hooter sounded. With their semifinal campaign over, India will now turn their attention to the classification playoff, where they will face co-hosts Belgium in the seventh-place match on Friday, August 28. India finished at the bottom of Pool E without a point, having also suffered a 3-1 defeat against the Netherlands.
For Fulton, however, the immediate focus will be on addressing India's struggles in high-pressure encounters.
“We played at a high level in tournament, but in the big games we have to do better,” the coach said, summing up a disappointing end to India's World Cup campaign.

stories.headline: Syndrela, set to become youngest Indian in 2026 Asiad, celebrates 17th B-day with two titles
stories.bodyText:
KOLKATA: Syndrela Das hates to travel on her birthday. But she made her 17th birthday away from home memorable by bagging a ‘double’ winning the Under-19 and women’s singles titles at the UTT National Ranking Table Tennis Championships that concluded in Kanpur on Sunday.
It was a day devoted totally on the board as the rising Bengal table tennis star played seven matches throughout the day without a defeat, beating Tamil Nadu’s Ananya Muralidharan 4-1 in the U-19 final and then overcoming Maharashtra’s Divyanshi Bhowmick 4-2 in a closely fought title-clash in the women’s final.
The victories could not have come at a better time for Das, who will become the youngest Indian athlete in the upcoming Asian Games a month later. Das, who finished runner-up at the Senior Nationals in Indore in March, had to toil hard to edge past PSPB’s Swastika Ghosh 4-3 (11-9, 5-11, 11-8, 8-11, 11-8, 8-11, 11-9) in the women’s semifinal. In a topsy-turvy battle, Das was trailing 4-7 in the decider before recovering to seal the match 11-9.
Das had to bring her best against her friend and biggest rival on the domestic circuit Bhowmick in the final as the Maharashtra paddler won the opening game 11-9. 
Das responded with two straight games but Bhowmick levelled at 2-2 with an 11-5 win in the fourth game, only for Das to regain the lead winning the fifth 11-7. She then held her nerve in a tight sixth game to bag the title.
However, the U-19 final went much smoother for Das.

briefs.headline: Playing Test cricket is a privilege: Jurel
briefs.deck: When Sri Lanka turned up for the first innings, Dhruv Jurel donned the wicket-keeping gloves
briefs.bodyText:
Time seemingly paused as Dhruv Jurel batted on 99. With Mohammed Siraj for company, and an anxious Indian camp watching from the dressing room, Jurel took 13 deliveries to move to his coveted hundred while surviving a run out attempt too in the process. His knock deflated host Sri Lanka in the second Test.
Speaking to the media in Colombo on Monday (August 24, 2026) and recalling that nervous-nineties phase, Jurel said: “So actually, when I was on 99, before that I was getting runs, and on 99, he (Asitha Fernando) started bowling good lengths. When I played that shot (for the hundred), thought it was going past the fielder, that there was a gap, and then I was like oh God!”
On a stop-start day due to the rains, Jurel seemed at ease, and he explained: “I am used to it because I was here with India A and am aware of the situation, about the (rain) breaks. I was just trying to bat in partnerships and also assess the conditions. Even if I scored a 100 today, tomorrow I will go and start from zero, that’s how it is.”
When Sri Lanka turned up for the first innings, Jurel donned the wicket-keeping gloves. Clarifying that move, he said: “Right now, (Rishabh) Pant has a sore right shoulder. We are closely monitoring him. Today I kept wickets, hopefully he will be fit.”
Among the rivals, Jurel lauded Asitha: “It was so hot and he used the short ball. It’s not easy for a bowler, and he was really challenging, especially when I was on 99.” Stressing that playing red-ball cricket is important, Jurel said: “Playing Test cricket is a privilege. We want to play well both in white and in blue.”
Published - August 25, 2026 03:31 am IST

briefs.headline: Cummins eyes ODI return ahead of ‘big’ South Africa Test series
briefs.deck: The next assignment for Australia after drawing a two-Test series against Bangladesh are three ODIs in Zimbabwe and another three in South Africa in late September
briefs.bodyText:
Skipper Pat Cummins said he “can’t wait” to play in Australia’s first Test series in South Africa since the infamous “Sandpapergate” affair, and he intends to use one-day games beforehand to prepare.
The next assignment for Australia after drawing a two-Test series against Bangladesh is three ODIs in Zimbabwe and another three in South Africa in late September.
They then play Tests in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town in October.
Cummins indicated he could miss the Zimbabwe leg, but would make himself available for some of the South Africa white-ball games.
It is likely to be a similar scenario for fellow quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.
“I’m not sure I should say this, but I think the focus is on the Test series,” said Cummins after their innings and 51-run thrashing of Bangladesh in Mackay on Sunday (August 23, 2026).
“So a lot of the white-ball (series), and how we play that, would be with an eye to the red ball.” “So I’d imagine it’d be one, two, probably a maximum of three games out of those six.”
Cummins, who remains Australia’s official ODI captain, has played just two from a possible 28 matches in the format since the 2023 World Cup.
Hazlewood told reporters in Mackay he too expected to play some of the 50-over series while Starc said he would “do what he’s told”.
All three have prioritised Tests over limited-overs cricket in recent years.
The Tests in South Africa will be Australia’s first in the country since a 2018 ball-tampering scandal rocked the sport.
Steve Smith was banned for a year and sacked as captain after conspiring to alter the ball using sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town, while David Warner was suspended for 12 months.
Cummins called the series “big” with revenge on his mind after Australia lost the World Test Championship final to the Proteas at Lord’s last year.
“We had a big series against them a couple of years ago in Australia (in 2022-23) and we probably exceeded expectations and played really well,” said Cummins of their 2-0 series win.
“They got us back at Lord’s last year and outplayed us. So it’s going to be big in their home conditions and places we have haven’t played for quite a while.
“Even the difference between Durban to, say, Cape Town can be quite different styles of pitches.
“That’s why I love playing Test cricket. It’s all different conditions, different opponents, different parts of the world. Can’t wait.”
Only Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood, Smith, Nathan Lyon, and Matt Renshaw have played Test cricket in South Africa.
Opener Renshaw is likely to hold his place despite a tepid return in Mackay after three years away, with the big question whether Marnus Labuschagne should be on the plane.
The number three made just 36 runs in three knocks against Bangladesh and has not scored a century since 2023.
“I did say a couple of days ago — and I think it still stands — that he’s been batting fantastically well off the field,” said Cummins. “But it doesn’t mean much. You’ve got to convert that into runs out there.”

briefs.headline: GCT Grand Finale: Praggnanandhaa beats Keymer to stake his claim for finals
briefs.deck: It was, at best can be described as a game of fluctuating fortunes wherein Pragg suffered early as white, wherein Keymer had the control and a legitimate shot at attacking the white king out of a Bishop’s opening by the Indian
briefs.bodyText:
Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa defeated Vincent Keymer of Germany to take a 9-3 lead and came close to qualifying for the finals of the concluding event of the Grand Chess Tour.
It was, at best can be described as a game of fluctuating fortunes wherein Pragg suffered early as white, wherein Keymer had the control and a legitimate shot at attacking the white king out of a Bishop’s opening by the Indian.
However, Caissa had other plans in store despite Pragg’s early slips as Keymer fell for a tactical trick that netted him a rook for a knight but the position turned in favour of the Indian leaving an advanced passed pawn in addition to black’s rook entrapment.
With both players running out of time, Keymer found a way to continue but it was in the second time control wherein Pragg showed little lenience and was close to checkmating the king when Keymer resigned on his 55th move.
The victory meant that Pragg is now only six points away from making it to the finals of the $450000 tournament, wherein $200000 is reserved for the winner.
There will be two more rapid games in which four points are reserved for the winner and four blitz games that give two points for winning a game. Normally the 9-3 lead that Pragg has could be the deciding factor in the mini-match.
In the other semifinal, Fabiano Caruana of United States must be cursing his stars as he let slip a winning position out of hands against compatriot Wesley So. Right from the beginning of a Berlin defense, Caruana called the shots and showcased a brilliant preparation that led to a huge advantage as the dust settled.
Wesley was outplayed right from the opening but the fighter in him put him afloat in a jungle of variations. Facing a massacre, the Filipino-turned-American decided to put up a brave front and capitalized on some judgmental erros by Caruana to reach a drawn King and pawns endgame. The game lasted 50 moves.
In the grand finale a total of 28 points are at stake and anyone who scores 15 points qualifies to the finals while the losing semifinalist will play against each other to determine the third place finisher.
The top three from here will also get a direct invite to next year’s Grand Chess tour and the winner from this event will walk home with 200000 USD. The second placed will earn $125000, third will go home richer by $75000 while the one finishing last will take away $50000.
Results round 2 Classical: R. Praggnanandhaa (Ind, 9) beat Vincent Keymer (Ger, 3); Fabiano Caruana (Usa, 6) drew with Wesley So (Usa, 6).

briefs.headline: ​Perfect host: On India as host of the 2026 BWF World Championships
briefs.deck: India was successful as a host of badminton World Championships
briefs.bodyText:
The 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi marked the rise of France as an on-court force and of India as a capable host. Alex Lanier’s triumph in singles, and Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue’s in mixed doubles, were the first golds in France’s history. It was just over three months ago that the European nation finished a worthy runner-up to China in the Thomas Cup, the de facto World Cup in badminton. The Worlds success has established France as a serious contender in a sport otherwise dominated by Asian countries. In fact, Lanier is just the third non-Asian this century — after Spain’s Carolina Marin and Denmark’s Viktor Axelsen — to win the singles gold at the World Championships. The 21-year-old did that at a spruced-up Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, which was in the dock earlier in January when pigeons and monkeys intruded into the arena during the India Open. The massive facelift ensured that the marquee event’s return to India after 17 years would be long remembered. An Se-Young will also go back with happy memories after reclaiming the women’s singles crown from three-time titlist Akane Yamaguchi. The victory extended the 24-year-old reigning Olympic champion’s stellar 2026, during which she has won an Uber Cup gold medal, and the individual and team trophies at the Badminton Asia Championships.
For India, the competition was the 12th straight edition where it secured at least one medal, with Gayatri Gopichand and Treesa Jolly bagging a bronze in women’s doubles. The performance is the latest in a series of good outcomes for Indian badminton after an ordinary 2025, where Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty’s World Championships doubles bronze was the best result. This year, Lakshya Sen reached the All England Open final, and Ayush Shetty at the Badminton Asia Championships. P.V. Sindhu’s victory at the Japan Open Super 750 last month was only her second Tour title in the last four years, and there were also triumphs for Satwiksairaj and Chirag at Singapore Open Super 750, and for Devika Sihag, Tanvi Sharma and Ashmita Chaliha at the Super 300 level. Yet, the feeling is unmistakable that India should have done better at a home World Championships, with Lakshya’s second-round defeat to the unheralded American teenager Garret Tan the most disappointing. There is no questioning the 25-year-old’s capability; he is a World Championships bronze medallist, a two-time All England finalist and finished an agonising fourth at the Paris 2024 Olympics. But no Indian men’s singles player has won an elite BWF Super 1000-level title since K. Srikanth in 2017. A swift end to this drought is essential for the overall health of the sport.

briefs.headline: KCL | Harikrishnan and Rohan delight in Globstars’ easy win
briefs.bodyText:
It was a perfect Monday for Calicut Globstars captain Rohan S. Kunnummal. He won an important toss and saw his bowlers exploit the conditions to bundle out Alleppey Ripples for an under-par total of 131. Rohan then rode his luck during the chase, dropped on three and 49 by Akshay Pillai, to smash a blistering 47-ball 94 (6x4, 8x6) to turn the run chase into a breeze.
Calicut’s win was set up by left-arm spinner M.U. Harikrishnan, whose double-wicket maiden over delivered a sucker punch from which Ripples never really recovered. He scalped Jalaj Saxena and skipper Sachin Baby off successive deliveries in the second over of the innings to push Ripples onto the back foot.
Early strikes
Akhil Scaria tightened the screws by dismissing the in-form Mohammed Azharuddeen (16) and K.A. Arun in the third over to leave Ripples struggling at 16 for four. There was a brief recovery when Abhijith Praveen (24) and Sibin Girish (17) added 30 runs for the eighth wicket. Ashiq Ali’s cameo at the end (33 not out, 17b, 4x4, 1x6) boosted the total.
Jalaj Saxena struck twice in the PowerPlay to reduce Globstars to 18 for two to give Ripples hope. However, Rohan capitalised on his early lifeline and batted aggressively to put the Ripples bowlers under pressure. Rohan, who celebrated a second reprieve by clubbing Ajinas for three consecutive sixes, missed out on a century while trying another big hit, but Akhil Scaria (31 not out) was there to guide Globstars home.
In the second match, Trivandrum Royals registered its first win by crushing defending champion Kochi Blue Tigers by 55 runs. All-rounder Sijomon Joseph spanked an unbeaten 56 to propel Royals to 185 for six.
Tigers were never in the hunt after losing early wickets in the PowerPlay and ended up scoring 130 for nine. Sijomon did his part with the ball also by grabbing two for 20 as the Tigers slumped to their third straight defeat.
The scores: Alleppey Ripples 131 in 19.3 overs (Ashiq Ali 33, M.U. Harikrishnan 3/12, Vignesh Puthur 2/25, Akhil Scaria 2/27) lost to Calicut Globstars 135/4 in 16.5 overs (Rohan Kunnummal 94, Akhil Scaria 31 n.o., Abhijith Praveen 2/8, Jalaj Saxena 2/13).

briefs.headline: SL vs IND 2nd Test, Day 2: Jurel and Pant turn up the heat on rain-hit day
briefs.deck: The two add 112 for the seventh wicket as India declares its first innings at 503 for nine; Sri Lanka tottering at eight for two in reply
briefs.bodyText:
The afternoon turned grim, dark clouds hung low, skyscrapers became silhouettes and vanished entirely from view. The rain was that intense, cascading in waves, just like how Arundhati Roy wrote in The God of Small Things: “Slanting silver ropes slammed into loose earth, ploughing it like gunfire.”
The liquid intervention at 2.13 p.m. lasted 23 minutes. The efficient ground staff at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground covered the entire turf in sheets and the venue was not ploughed. But the showers forced a break during the second Test’s second day at a time when India was coasting against Sri Lanka.
Gradually the clouds receded, the sun emerged and play resumed at 4.22 p.m., with India placed on 475 for eight and Dhruv Jurel on 95. He took his time, was stationary on 99 for a while before scampering for a single after tapping Asitha Fernando towards mid-off. Later he hoisted the seamer for a big six.
Even as Mohammed Siraj left and last-man Prasidh Krishna appeared, Jurel (115 n.o., 177b, 9x4, 2x6) ensured that India crossed 500. Aptly Shubman Gill declared the first innings at 503 for nine. At close, Sri Lanka was struggling at eight for two with Yashasvi Jaiswal’s diving catch to terminate Lahiru Udara’s stint being the highlight.
India’s batting effort rested entirely on two wicketkeeper-batters — the maverick Rishabh Pant and the efficient Jurel. Their 112-run seventh-wicket partnership anchored India past the 400-mark. Pant (63, 89b, 6x4, 2x6) fell off the first ball after lunch, while trying to clear long-off against off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha.
Jurel, though, remained calm. He accumulated runs at a steady trot even as Manav Suthar flickered a while before edging left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya. After Siraj walked in, Jurel held onto the strike as much as he could while the former defended. Jurel on-drove Asitha for four and then the skies opened up.
Earlier, resuming at 300 for five, India lost Saransh Jain as he awkwardly fended a short-pitched delivery from Asitha. But there were no Monday morning blues as Pant, who had retired hurt on the opening day, returned.
Lahiru Kumara steamed in and pitched it short around the leg-stump. Pant just swivelled and pulled a massive six that hit the roof. While Jurel remained patient, Pant was busy.
Host skipper Dhananjaya de Silva placed fielders at fine-leg, third-man, backward square-leg and sweeper-cover. Pacers, be it Asitha or Kumara, ran in and bounced, hoping for a miscued hit. Pant remained unruffled, and suffered a few blows too as he ducked and weaved.
He pinched some fours off Nuwantha while Jurel pulled Asitha past the ropes. Prabath found Pant drilling one straight down the ground and soon the batter reached his 50. Jurel too followed suit and then Pant whipped a six off Prabath over mid-wicket as India moved to 419 for six at lunch.
Pant dominated the first act, and it was time for Jurel to flourish in the second part. He precisely did that for his second Test century.

briefs.headline: Rain plays spoilsport again; Kovai Kings progress to TNPL Qualifier 2
briefs.bodyText:
Vida Kovai Kings progressed to Qualifier 2 of the TNPL after its Eliminator against iDream Tiruppur Tamizhans was washed out at the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium here on Monday.
Kovai Kings and Tamizhans were placed third and fourth on the table, with both teams on eight points. But Kovai Kings had the superior Net Run Rate of 1.638, compared to Tamizhans’ -0.013, and thus advanced to the next stage.
The match had promised intriguing battles, with the Shahrukh Khan-led side boasting the tournament’s two most economical bowlers in left-arm spinner M. Siddharth (nine wickets at 5.46) and leggie Jhathavedh Subramanyan (13 at 6.29).
Tamizhans’ openers Amith Sathvik (striking at 212.74) and left-hander Tushar Raheja (193.08) arrived as the competition’s two fastest-scoring batters.
Kovai Kings’ pace duo of Deeban Lingesh (12) and G. Kishoor (10) had also been among the wickets, providing further edge to the Eliminator.
Asked to bat, Tamizhans made an unusually sedate start, reaching 15 without loss in three overs before a heavy downpour brought play to a halt.
Deeban, bowling with the wicketkeeper standing up to the stumps, and Siddharth kept things tight, denying the openers the kind of start they had become accustomed to this season.

briefs.headline: Hockey World Cup: India crashes out after another lacklustre show
briefs.deck: Argentina punishes the former champion for its defensive errors
briefs.bodyText:
Sukhjeet Singh put his arms aloft in celebration after scoring a goal in the 57th minute. But it was his side’s second to Argentina’s five as its World Cup run was nearing the end. It summed up India’s day at the Wagener Stadion on Monday.
Twenty three years ago, it was in this very arena, where India scripted one of its greatest comebacks, overturning a 2-4 deficit in 15 minutes to beat Pakistan 7-4 in the Champions Trophy. Needing a big win to stay alive in the men’s World Cup, there was to be no repeat story from the current class as it went down 5-3.
A sloppy display from Craig Fulton’s men , keeping with this team’s run so far in 2026, was picked apart by a ruthless Argentina. The defeat was India’s third in five games in this World Cup. The former champion also let in 16 goals — the most it has conceded since the 2010 edition. Finishing last in Pool E, India will play the seventh-place classification game against Belgium.
India got off to a dreadful start as Argentina capitalised on its defensive errors.
Inside 40 seconds, a failed clearance allowed an unmarked Joaquin Toscani slot home for the first.
Four minutes later, indecision from Yashdeep Siwach resulted in the defender conceding a penalty corner, which Nicolas Della Torre pushed low and hard to make it 2-0.
India found a lifeline through Sukhjeet as he scored with a backhand finish.
Better control prevailed in the second quarter before further mistakes proved to be India’s undoing once again. Mohith H.S. could do nothing to stop Tomas Domene’s fiercely-struck reverse-hit.
Yashdeep’s day got only worse when his backpass was intercepted inside the 25 yards before the resulting shot on target struck his foot. Domene made no mistake from the spot to make it 4-1. With eight minutes to go, Lucas Toscani , under little pressure from Sanjay Rana, added a fifth from a tight angle.
A late resurgence saw India reduce the margin with another goal from Sukhjeet deflecting in a slapshot from Mandeep Singh before Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke.
Semifinal line-up
Argentina progressed to the semifinals after England could only manage a 2-2 draw with the Netherlands later in the day. The Dutch will meet Spain in Friday’s first semifinal while Argentina takes on Germany on the same day.
The result: Argentina 5 (Joaquin Toscani 1, Della Torre 5-pc, Domene 32 & 44-ps, Lucas Toscani 52) bt India 3 (Sukhjeet 9 & 57, Hardik 60-ps).
